contents.html:
trusted computing base (TCB)
1) The totality of protection mechanisms within a computer system including hardware, firmware, and software - the combination of which are responsible for enforcing a security policy. A TCB consists of one or more components that together enforce a unified security policy over a product or system. The ability of a TCB to correctly enforce a security policy depends solely on the mechanisms within the TCB and on the correct input by system administrative personnel of parameters (e.g., a user's clearance) related to the security policy. (DOD 5200,28-STD; AFR 205-16)
contents.html_ja:
trusted computing base (TCB)
1) ハードウェア、ファームウェア、ソフトウェアを含む、コンピュータシステム内の保護機構の全体で、その組合せがセキュリティポリシーの実施に責任を負うもの。TCB は、製品またはシステムに対して統一的なセキュリティポリシーを共同で実施する、一つ以上の構成要素から成ります。TCB がセキュリティポリシーを正しく実施する能力は、TCB 内の機構と、システム管理要員によるセキュリティポリシーに関連するパラメータ（例: 利用者のクリアランス）の正しい入力のみに依存します。（DOD 5200,28-STD; AFR 205-16）
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p165: 画像と語ごとに照合。用語と定義の断片を 1 項目にまとめる
contents.translation_resolve_note: 指摘は別のブロックについてのもので、修正案は現訳と同一

contents.html: 2) The totality of protection mechanisms within a computer system, including hardware firmware, and software, the combination of which is responsible for enforcing a security policy. A TCB consists of one or more components that together enforce a unified security policy over a product or system. The ability of a TCB to enforce correctly a unified security policy depends solely on the mechanisms within the TCB and on the correct input by system adminstrative personnel of parameters (e.g., a user's clearance level) related to the security policy. (NCSC-TG-004-88)
contents.html_ja: 2) ハードウェア、ファームウェア、ソフトウェアを含む、コンピュータシステム内の保護機構の全体で、その組合せがセキュリティポリシーの実施に責任を負うもの。TCB は、製品またはシステムに対して統一的なセキュリティポリシーを共同で実施する、一つ以上の構成要素から成ります。TCB が統一的なセキュリティポリシーを正しく実施する能力は、TCB 内の機構と、システム管理要員によるセキュリティポリシーに関連するパラメータ（例: 利用者のクリアランスレベル）の正しい入力のみに依存します。（NCSC-TG-004-88）

contents.html:
trusted distribution
A trusted method for distributing the TCB hardware, software, and firmware components, both originals and updates, that provides methods for protecting the TCB from modification during distribution and for detection of any changes to the TCB that may occur. (NCSC-TG-004-88)
contents.html_ja:
trusted distribution
TCB のハードウェア、ソフトウェア、ファームウェアの構成要素（原本と更新の両方）を配布するための信頼できる方法で、配布中の改変から TCB を保護する方法と、TCB に生じうる変更を検知する方法を提供するもの。（NCSC-TG-004-88）

contents.html:
trusted facility manual
This manual documents the operational requirements, security environment, hardware and software configuration, and interfaces; all security procedures, measures, and features; and, the contingency plans for computer facilities for continued support in case of local disaster. (AFR 205-16)
contents.html_ja:
trusted facility manual
このマニュアルは、運用要件、セキュリティ環境、ハードウェアとソフトウェアの構成、インタフェース、すべてのセキュリティ手順、対策、機能、および局地的な災害の場合に支援を継続するための、計算機施設の緊急時計画を文書化したものです。（AFR 205-16）

contents.html:
trusted identification forwarding
1) An identification method used in networks where the sending host can verify that an authorized user on its system is attempting a connection to another host. The sending host transmits tne required user authentication information to the receiving host. The receiving host can then verify that the user is validated for access to its system. This operation may be transparent to the user. (CSC-STD-002-85)
contents.html_ja:
trusted identification forwarding
1) ネットワークで用いられる識別方法で、送信側ホストが、自らのシステム上の認可された利用者が、別のホストへの接続を試みていることを検証できるもの。送信側ホストは、必要な利用者認証情報を受信側ホストに送信します。その後、受信側ホストは、その利用者が自らのシステムへのアクセスについて検証されていることを確認できます。この操作は、利用者に気づかれずに行われる場合があります。（CSC-STD-002-85）

contents.html: 2) An identification method used in networks whereby the sending host can verify that an authorized user on its system is attempting a connection to another host. The sending host transmits the required user authentication information to the receiving host. The receiving host can then verify that the user is validated for access to its system. This operation may be transparent to the user. (NCSC-TG-004-88)
contents.html_ja: 2) ネットワークで用いられる識別方法で、これにより、送信側ホストが、自らのシステム上の認可された利用者が、別のホストへの接続を試みていることを検証できるもの。送信側ホストは、必要な利用者認証情報を受信側ホストに送信します。その後、受信側ホストは、その利用者が自らのシステムへのアクセスについて検証されていることを確認できます。この操作は、利用者に対して透過的である場合があります。（NCSC-TG-004-88）

contents.html:
trusted network interface
A special-purpose device placed between the network and other devices using the network. (AFR 205-16)
contents.html_ja:
trusted network interface
ネットワークと、そのネットワークを使用する他の装置との間に置かれる、専用装置。（AFR 205-16）

contents.html:
trusted path
A mechanism by which a person at a terminal can communicate directly with the trusted computing base. This mechanism can only be activated by the person or the trusted computing base and cannot be imitated by untrusted software. (DOD 5200.28-STD)
contents.html_ja:
trusted path
端末にいる人が、トラステッドコンピューティングベースと直接通信できるようにする機構。この機構は、その人またはトラステッドコンピューティングベースのみが起動でき、信頼されないソフトウェアによって模倣することはできません。（DOD 5200.28-STD）

contents.html:
trusted process
1) A process which can affect system security. It is sometimes but not always endowed with privileges to override kernel-enforced rules. The protection capabilities or characteristics of a trusted process must be reliably demonstrated to comply with stated requirements, through formal verification when possible. Trusted processes are sometimes used to execute NKSR software. (MTR-8201)
contents.html_ja:
trusted process
1) システムのセキュリティに影響を及ぼしうるプロセス。カーネルが実施する規則を無効にする特権を与えられている場合もありますが、常にそうとは限りません。信頼されたプロセスの保護能力または特性は、可能な場合は形式検証によって、規定の要件に準拠していることが確実に実証されなければなりません。信頼されたプロセスは、NKSR ソフトウェアの実行に用いられることがあります。（MTR-8201）
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p166: 画像と語ごとに照合。用語と定義の断片を 1 項目にまとめる

contents.html: 2) A process whose incorrect or malicious execution is capable of violating system security policy. (NCSC-TG-004-88)
contents.html_ja: 2) その不正確なまたは悪意ある実行が、システムのセキュリティポリシーに違反しうるプロセス。（NCSC-TG-004-88）
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p167: 画像と語ごとに照合。文字層に無い番号「2)」を画像から補う

contents.html:
trusted products
Products evaluated and approved for inclusion on tne Evaluated Products List (EPL). (DODD 5200.28)
contents.html_ja:
trusted products
評価され、Evaluated Products List（EPL）への掲載を承認された製品。（DODD 5200.28）

contents.html:
trusted software

contents.html_ja:
trusted software

trusted system
取扱注意の情報源と情報収集方法を伴う情報機関の情報の処理に使用できるようにするために、十分な完全性対策を採用したもの。（DCID 1/16, Sup.）

twit

twit
システムを適切に使用できない、または使用しようとしない利用者。この種の利用者に対する反応は、通常は厳しく、アクセスの拒否や、その地域の他の SYSOP への通知を含みます。（BBD）

contents.html:
two person integrity (TPI)

特定の COMSEC 鍵素材へのアクセスを禁止するために設計された、保管と取扱いの方式で、少なくとも二人の正式に認可された者の立会いを求め、各自が、実行されている作業に関する不正確なまたは不正なセキュリティ手順を検知できるようにするもの。（NTISSI 3004）

type1 magnetic media

contents.html_ja:

contents.html:
unclassified information
Any information that need not be safeguarded against disclosure, but must be safeguarded against tampering, destruction, or loss due to record value, utility, replacement cost or susceptibility to fraud, waste, or abuse. (DODD 5200.28)
contents.html_ja:

contents.html:
unclassified telecommunications security
That domain of unclassified computer security that is concerned with protecting the point-to-point communication (e.g., input device to computer, computer to computer) of sensitive unclassified information with appropriate cost-effective measures (e.g., data encryption and protected distribution systems). Such communications generally occur via data communication systems, links, and devices such as networks, local area networks, telephone/wire lines, fiber optics, raoio waves/microwaves, and integrated circuits. (DOE 1360.2A)
contents.html_ja:
unclassified telecommunications security
取扱注意の非機密情報のポイントツーポイント通信（例: 入力装置からコンピュータ、コンピュータからコンピュータ）を、適切で費用対効果の高い対策（例: データ暗号化や保護された配布システム）で保護することに関わる、非機密コンピュータセキュリティの領域。このような通信は、一般に、ネットワーク、ローカルエリアネットワーク、電話線/有線回線、光ファイバー、電波/マイクロ波、集積回路などのデータ通信システム、リンク、装置を介して行われます。（DOE 1360.2A）

contents.html:
verifiable identification forwarding
1) An identification method used in networks where the sending host can verify that an authorized user on its system is attempting a connection to another host. The sending host transmits the required user authentication information to the receiving host. The receiving host can then verify that the user is validated for access to its system. This operation may be transparent to the user. (DOE 5637.1)
contents.html_ja:
verifiable identification forwarding
1) ネットワークで用いられる識別方法で、送信側ホストが、自らのシステム上の認可された利用者が、別のホストへの接続を試みていることを検証できるもの。送信側ホストは、必要な利用者認証情報を受信側ホストに送信します。その後、受信側ホストは、その利用者が自らのシステムへのアクセスについて検証されていることを確認できます。この操作は、利用者に対して透過的である場合があります。（DOE 5637.1）

contents.html:
virus
1) A variation of Trojan horse. It attaches itself to files or programs with a triggering mechanism (event, time) with a mission to delete files or send data. Protection from a virus is beyond the criteria set forth in DOD Standard 5200.28-STD, DOD Trusted Computer System Evaluation Criteria. (AFR 205-10)
contents.html_ja:
virus
1) トロイの木馬の一種。ファイルの削除やデータの送信を任務として、起動の仕組み（事象、時刻）を持つファイルまたはプログラムに、自らを付着させます。ウイルスからの保護は、DOD Standard 5200.28-STD、DOD Trusted Computer System Evaluation Criteria に定められた基準の範囲を超えています。（AFR 205-10）

vulnerability
1) 不正な情報アクセスや重要な処理の妨害に脅威が悪用する可能性のある、自動化システムのセキュリティ手順、管理策、内部統制などの弱点。（AFR 700-10; AR 380-380）

contents.html: 2) Characteristics of a friendly telecommunications system or cryptosystem which are potentially exploitable by hostile intelligence entities. (NCSC-9)

contents.html: 3) The susceptibility of a particular system to a specific attack, along with the opportunity available to a hostile entity to mount that attack. (JCS PUB 6-03.7)
contents.html_ja: 3) 特定のシステムが特定の攻撃に対して持つ感受性と、敵対的なエンティティがその攻撃を仕掛けるために利用できる機会。脆弱性は常に実証可能ですが、既知の脅威とは独立して存在する場合があります。一般に、脆弱性の記述は、友軍の管理下にある要因を考慮に入れます。（JCS PUB 6-03.7）

contents.html: 4) A weakness in the physical layout, organization, procedures, personnel, management, administration, hardware, or software that may be exploited to cause harm to the ADP system or activity. contents.html:
wiretapping
1) Cutting in on a communications line to get information.
a. Active. The attaching of an unauthorized device, such as a computer terminal, to a communications circuit for the purpose of obtaining access to data through the generation of false messages or control signals, or by altering the communications of legitimate users.
b. Passive. The monitoring and/or recording of data which is being transmitted over a communication link. (AR 380-380)
contents.html_ja:
wiretapping
1) 情報を得るために、通信回線に割り込むこと。
a. 能動的。偽のメッセージまたは制御信号の生成、または正規の利用者の通信の改変によって、データへのアクセスを得る目的で、コンピュータ端末などの不正な装置を通信回線に接続すること。
b. 受動的。通信リンクを通じて送信されているデータを監視および/または記録すること。（AR 380-380）

Preface

This National Institute of Standards and Technology Interagency Report (NISTIR) presents a glossary of computer security terminology, whose development was sponsored under the auspices of the National Security Telecommunications and Information Systems Security Committee (NSTISSC) This glossary is a collection of . terms and definitions used by various federal departments and agencies in their policies, standards, and other publications. This glossary did not seek to arrive at a single agreed-upon definition of each entry; therefore, some definitions may not be wholly consistent. Although never formally issued by the NSTISSC, since the document does reflect actual usage of these terms, it may provide a useful reference source to the computer security practitioner

The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) makes no claim or endorsement of this glossary. However, as this material may be of use to other organizations, it is being reprinted by NIST to provide for broad public dissemination of this federally sponsored work. This publication is part of a continuing effort to assist federal agencies in accordance with NIST's mandate under the Computer Security Act of 1987.

computer abuse

1) Willful or negligent unauthorized activity that affects the availability, confidentiality, or integrity of computer resources. Computer abuse includes fraud, embezzlement, theft, malicious damage, unauthorized use, denial of service, and misappropriation. Levels of computer abuse are:
a. Minor Abuse - Acts that represent management problems (printing calendars or running games), but do not impact system availability for authorized applications;
b. Major Abuse - Unauthorized use (possibly criminal), resulting in denial of service, multiple instances of minor abuse, or waste;

subject maintains a list of unforgeable bit patterns, called tickets, one for each object the subject is authorized to access. (NCSC-TG-004-88)
time bomb/
In computer security, a variant of the Trojan horse in which malicious code is inserted to be
time-bomb
triggered later. (MS; JCS PUB 6-03.7)
time-dependent password
A password which is valid only at a certain time
of day or during a specified interval of time. (AR 380-380; FIPS PUB 39)
top-level
A non-procedural description of system behavior
specification (TLS)
at the most abstract level. Typically functional
specification that omits all implementation details. (DOD 5200.28-STD)
traffic analysis
1) The study of communications characteristics
which are external to the encrypted texts. (NCSC-9)
2) The process of deducing information from the nature of the traffic on a network (message frequency, message length, etc.) rather than having knowledge of the actual data being transmitted. (WB)
traffic flow
Any information which reveals the presence or
information
absence of a legitimate message within a given
time period. (NACSEM 5201)
traffic flow
1) The protection that results from those features
security
in some crypto-equipment that conceal the

presence of valid messages on a communications circuit. This is usually done by causing the circuit to appear busy at all times, or by encrypting the source and destination addresses of valid messages. (FIPS PUB 39; AR 380-380)
2) The capability of certain on-line, machine-cryptosystems to conceal the presence of valid traffic. (NCSC-9)
tranquility
1) A security model rule stating that the security
level of an active object cannot change during the period of activity. (MTR-8201)
2) A security model rule stating that the security level of an object cannot change while the object is being processed by an AIS. (NCSC-TG-004-88)
trap door
1) A hidden software or hardware mechanism
that responds to a special input which is used to circumvent security controls. (AFR 205- 1 6)

2) A condition existing in the system software or hardware which can be triggered to subvert the software or hardware security features. Basically, the condition Is prompted internally (such as, by a counter, a date or time value, or any specific set of preestablished circumstances) or externally (such as, by a remote terminal or application program input message). (AR 380-380)

3) A hidden software or hardware mechanism that permits system protection mechanisms to be circumvented. It is activated In some non-apparent manner (e.g. special "random" key sequence at a terminal). (DOD 5200.28-STD)
4) A breach created Intentionally in an ADP system for the purpose of collecting, altering or destroying data. (FIPS PUB 39)

A hidden software or hardware mechanism 5) that permits system protection mechanisms to be circumvented. It is activated in some innocent-appearing manner (e.g., special "random" key sequence at a terminal). Software developers often introduce trap doors in their code that enable them to re-enter the system and perform certain functions. (NCSC-TG-004-88)
Trojan horse
A program containing hidden code which
1) allows the unauthorizecTcollection, falsification, or destruction of data. (AFR 205-16)

A computer program with an apparently or 2) actually useful function that contains additional (hidden) functions that surreptitiously exploit the legitimate authorizations of the invoking process to the detriment of security. For example, making a " blind copy" of a sensitive file for the creator of the Trojan horse. (DOD 5200.28-STD)
3) actually useful and that contains a trap door. (FIPS PUB 39; AR 380-380)
A computer program that apparently or
is

A computer program with an apparently or 4) actually useful function that contains additional (hidden) functions that surreptitiously exploit the legitimate authorizations of the invoking process to the detriment of security or integrity. (NCSC-TG-004-88)
trusted computer system
1) A system that employs sufficient hardware and
software integrity measures to allow its use for simultaneous processing of multiple levels of classified and/or sensitive information. (AR 380-380; DOD 5200.28-STD; DODD 5225.1)
2) A system that employs sufficient hardware and software assurance measures to allow its use for simultaneous processinq of a range of sensitive or classified information. {NCSC-TG-004)
trusted computing
1) The totality of protection mechanisms within a
base (TCB)
computer system including hardware, firmware,

and software - the combination of which are responsible for enforcing a security policy. A TCB consists of one or more components that together enforce a unified security policy over a product or system. The ability of a TCB to correctly enforce a security policy depends solely on the mechanisms within the TCB and on the correct input by system administrative personnel of parameters (e.g., a user's clearance) related to the security policy. (DOD 5200,28-STD; AFR 205-16)

2) The totality of protection mechanisms within a computer system, including hardware firmware, and software, the combination of which is responsible for enforcing a security policy. A TCB consists of one or more components that together enforce a unified security policy over a product or system. The ability of a TCB to enforce correctly a unified security policy depends solely on the mechanisms within the TCB and on the correct input by system adminstrative personnel of parameters (e.g., a user's clearance level) related to the security policy. (NCSC-TG-004-88)
trusted distribution
A trusted method for distributing the TCB

hardware, software, and firmware components, both originals and updates, that provides methods for protecting the TCB from modification during distribution and for detection of any changes to the TCB that may occur. (NCSC-TG-004-88)
trusted facility manual
This manual documents the operational

requirements, security environment, hardware and software configuration, and interfaces; all security procedures, measures, and features; and, the contingency plans for computer facilities for continued support in case of local disaster. (AFR205-16)
trusted
1) An identification method used in networks
identification
where the sending host can verify that an
forwarding
authorized user on its system is attempting a

connection to another host. The sending host transmits tne required user authentication information to the receiving host. The receiving host can then verify that the user is validated for access to its system. This operation may be transparent to the user. (CSC-STD-002-85)

2) An identification method used in networks whereby the sending host can verify that an authorized user on its system is attempting a connection to another host The sending host transmits the required user authentication information to the receiving host. The receiving host can then verify that the user is validated for access to its system. This operation may be transparent to the user. (NCSC-TG’004~88)
trusted network
A special-purpose device placed between the
interface
network and other devices using the network.
trusted path
A mechanism by which a person at a terminal can
communicate directly with the trusted computing base. This mechanism can only be activated by the person or the trusted computing base and cannot be imitated by untrusted software. (DOD 5200.28-STD)
trusted process
1) A process which can affect system security. It is

sometimes but not always endowed with privileges to override kernel-enforced rules. The protection capabilities or characteristics of a trusted process must be reliably demonstrated to comply with stated requirements, through formal verification when possible. Trusted processes are sometimes used to execute NKSR software. (MTR-8201)
A process whose incorrect or malicious execution is capable of violating system security policy. (NCSC-TG-004-88)
trusted products
Products evaluated and approved for inclusion on
tne Evaluated Products List (EPL). (DODD 5200.28)
trusted software
1) The software portion of a TCB that can be relied
upon to enforce security policy. (AFR 205-16)

2) Software, usually affecting system security, that has been certified to perform as specified. Certification may be performed by any organization the accreditor deems appropriate, depending on the situation. (JCS PUB 6-03.7)
3) The software portion of a trusted computing base. (DOD 5200.28-STD)
4) See TRUSTED PROCESS.
trusted system
Employing sufficient integrity measures to allow
its use for processing intelligence information involving sensitive intelligence sources and methods (DCID 1/16, Sup.)
twit
User who can not, or will not use the system
properly. Reactions to this type of user are usually severe, including denial of access and notification to other SYSOPs In the area. (BBD)
two person
A system of storage and handling designed to
integrity (TPI)
prohibit access to certain COMSEC keying material,
by requiring the presence of at least two formally authorized persons, each capable of detecting incorrect or unauthorized security procedures with respect to the task being performed. (NTISSI 3004)
typel magnetic media
Magnetic media with coercivity factors not
exceeding 3005 oersteds. {CSC-STD-005-85)
type2 magnetic
Magnetic media with coercivity factors exceeding
media
3005 oersteds, possibly as high as 750 oersteds
(also known as high energy media). (CSC-STD-005-85)
type
MAJCOM DAA
Official authorization by the
to
accreditation
employ a system in a specified operational

environment. This authorization includes a statement of residual risk, outlines the operating environment, and the system's specific use. This accreditation is optional when multiple copies of a system are to be fielded. {AFR 205-16; JCS PUB 6-03.7)
unapproved
All software that has not been formally identified, evaluated, and examined by competent
software
personnel to ensure that the software performs to exact specifications. (AR 380-380)
unclassified
Unclassified information whose unauthorized
controlled
dissemination is prohibited under section 148
nuclear information (UCNI)
of the Atomic Energy Act. (DOE 5635.1a)
unclassified
Any information that need not be safeguarded
information
against disclosure, but must be safeguarded
against tampering, destruction, or loss due to record value, utility, replacement cost or susceptibility to fraud, waste, or abuse. (DODD 5200.28)
unclassified telecommunications that concerned with protecting the Is
That domain of unclassified computer security
security
point-to-point communication (e.g.. Input device

to computer, computer to computer) of sensitive unclassified information with appropriate cost-effective measures (e.g., data encryption and protected distribution systems). Such communications generally occur via data communication systems, links, and devices such as networks, local area networks, telephone/wire lines, fiber optics, raoio waves/mIcrowaves, and integrated circuits. (DOE 1360. 2A)
uncontrolled
The area external or internal to a facility
access area (UAA)
over which no personnel access controls can be or
are exercised. (NACSIM 5203)
un protect
A software program which copies copy
1) protected software. Usually these programs are available before the "protected" product. (BBD)
See COPY PROTECTED. 2)
untrusted process
1) A process whose incorrect or malicious
execution cannot affect system security. Verification is usually not applied to untrusted processes. (MTR-8201)

A process that has not been evaluated or examined for adherence to the security policy. It may include incorrect or malicious code that attempts to circumvent the security mechanisms. (NCSC-TG-004~88)
user(s)
1) An organizational or programmatic entity that

receives service from an information technology facility. A user may be either internal or external to the agency organization responsible for the facility, but normally does not report to the manager or director of the facility or to the same Immediate supervisor. (A-130)
2) An Individual (person or organization) with direct access to the system or an individual without access who receives output or generates input not reviewed by another. {AFR 205-16; AFR 700-10)
3) Any authorized person, office, or staff agency who may use or receive services or products from a computer system. Synonymous with customer. (AR 380-380)
4) Any person who interacts directly with a computer system. (DOD 5200.28-STD)
5) A user Is an individual and/or processes operating on hIs/her/its behalf. (DCID 1/16, Sup.)

6) People or processes accessing an AIS either by direct connections (i.e., via terminals) or indirect connections (i.e., prepare input data or software or receive output that Is not reviewed for content and classification by a responsible individual). (DODD 5200.28)

7) Any individual who is able to operate any equipment that can access the ADP system or input commands to the ADP system or receive output from the ADP system without intervention of an authorized reviewing official. Note that a user may not necessarily be an authorized user of the ADP system. (DOE 5637.1)
8) A person or organization receiving products or services produced by an ADP system either by access to the system or by other means.
(OPNAVINST 5239.1 A)
user ID
A unique symbol or character string that is used by
a system to identify a specific user. (NCSC-TG-004-88)
user profile
Patterns of a user's activity that can be used to
detect changes in normal routines. (NCSC-TG-004-88)
U.S. nongovern-mental source
An individual citizen of the United States or a U.S.

corporation, association or other organization substantially composed of United States citizens, which is not directly a part of the government (for example, a self-employed individual, consulting firm, licensee, or contractor, excluding active or reserve military personnel. Civil Service employees, and other individuals employed directly by the government); specifically excluded are corporations or associations under foreign ownership, control, and influence. (NCSC-2)
validation
1) The performance of tests and evaluations In
order to determine compliance with security specifications and requirements. (FIPS PUB 39)

2) That portion of the development of specialized ST&E, procedures, tools, and equipment needed to establish acceptance for joint usage by one or more DOD components or their contractors. Such action will include, as necessary, final develop-ment, evaluation, and testing leading to acceptance, by senior ST&E staff specialists of the three military departments or a defense agency, and approval for joint usage by the appropriate DOD authority. (AR 380-380; DOD 5200. 28M;
OPNAVINST 5239.1 A)
valid password
A personal password that will authenticate the
identity of an individual when presented to a password system or an access password that will allow the requested access when presented to a password system. (FIPS PUB 112)
verifiable
1) An identification method used in networks
identification
where the sending host can verify that an
forwarding
authorized user on Its system is attempting a

connection to another host. The sending host transmits the required user authentication information to the receiving host. The receiving host can then verify that the user is validated for access to its system. This operation may be transparent to the user. (DOE 5637.1)
2) See TRUSTED IDENTIFICATION FORWARDING.
verification
1) The documentation of penetration or attempts
to penetrate an actual on-line system in support or in contradiction of assumptions developed during system review and analysis. (AR 380-380)

2) The successful testing and documentation of actual on-line system penetration or attempts to penetrate the system in support or in contradiction or assumptions developed during system review and analysis which are to be Included in the evaluation report.

3) The process of comparing two levels of system specification for proper correspondence (e.g., security policy model with top-level specification, TLS with source code, or source code with object code). This process may or may not be automated. (DOD 5200.28-STD)
virtual password
A password computed from a passphrase that
meets the requirements of password storage (e.g., 64 bits for DES). (FIPS PUB 112)
virus
1) A variation of Trojan horse. It attaches itself to
files or programs with a triggering mechanism (event, time) with a mission to delete files or send data. Protection from a virus is beyond the criteria
DOD
DOD
set forth in Standard 5200.28-STD, Trusted Computer System Evaluation Criteria. (AFR 205-10)
2) A self-propagating Trojan horse, composed of three parts: a mission component, a trigger component and a self-propagating component (NCSC-TG-004-88)
volatile memory
Memory (such as semiconductor memory) that
loses memory retention capability when electric power is removed. (JCS PUB 6-03.7)
vulnerability
1) A weakness in automated system security

procedures, administrative controls, internal controls, and so forth, that could be exploited by a threat to gain unauthorized access to information or disrupt critical processing. (AFR 700-10; AR 380-380)
2) Characteristics of a friendly telecommunications system or cryptosystem which are potentially exploitable by hostile intelligence entities. (NCSC-9)

3) The susceptibility of a particular system to a specific attack, along with the opportunity available to a hostile entity to mount that attack. A vulnerability is always demonstrable but may exist independently of a known threat. In general, a description of a vulnerability takes account of those factors under friendly control. (JCS PUB 6-03.7)

4) A weakness in the physical layout, organization, procedures, personnel, management, administration, hardware, or software that may be exploited to cause harm to the ADP system or activity. The presence of a vulnerability does not in itself cause harm; a vulnerability is merely a condition or set of conditions that may allow the ADP system or activity to be harmed by an attack.
(OPNAVINST 5239.1 A)

5) The characteristic of a system which causes it to suffer a definite degradation (inability to perform the designated mission) as a result of having been subjected to a certain level of effects in an unnatural (manmade) hostile environment. For computers, it is a weakness in automated systems security procedures, administrative controls, and so forth, that could be exploited to gain unauthorized access to information or disrupt critical processing. (AFR 205- 1 6)
6) A weakness in system security procedures, system design, implementation, internal controls, etc., that coul be exploited to violate system security policy. (NCSC‘TG-04-88)
vulnerability analysis The systematic examination of systems in order to
determine the adequacy of security measures, identify security deficiencies, and provide data from which to predict the efhctiveness of proposed security measures. (NCSC-TG-004-88)
vulnerability
1) A review of the susceptibility to loss or
assessment
unauthorized use of resources, errors in reports
and information, illegal or unethical acts, and/or adverse or unfavorable public opinion. (A-1 23)
2) A measurement of vulnerability which would include:
a. The susceptibility of a particular system to a specific attack.

b. The opportunity available to a threat agent (methods or things which may be used to exploit a vulnerability (such as fire)) to mount that attack. A vulnerability is always demonstrable but may exist independently of a known threat. In general, a description of a vulnerability takes account of those factors under friendly control. (AR 380-380)

3) A review of the susceptibility to loss or unauthorized use of resources, errors in reports and information, illegal or unethical acts, and adverse or unfavorable public opinion. Vulnerability assessments do not identify weaknesses or result in improvements. They are the mechanism with which an organization can determine quickly the potential for losses in its different programs or functions. The schedule of Internal control reviews should be based on the results of the vulnerability assessments. (DODD 7040.6)

4) The systematic examination of telecommunica-tions to determine the adequacy of COMSEC measures, to identify COMSEC deficiencies, to provide data from which to predict the effectiveness of proposed COMSEC measures, and to confirm the adequacy of such measures after implementation. (NCSC-9)

5) A measurement of vulnerability which includes the susceptibility of a particular system to a specific attack and the opportunities available to a threat agent to mount that attack. (NCSC-TG-004-88)
weapon data

Restricted data or formerly restricted data concerning the design, manufacture, or utilization (including theory, development, storage, characteristics, performance, and effects) of nuclear weapons or nuclear weapon components, including information incorporated in or related to nuclear explosive devices. (DOE 5635.1 A)
wiretapping
1) Cutting In on a communications line to get
Information.

a. Active. The attaching of an unauthorized device, such as a computer terminal, to a communications circuit for the purpose of obtaining access to data through the generation of false messages or control signals, or by altering the communications of legitimate users.
b. Passive. The monitoring and/or recording of data which is being transmitted over a communication link. (AR 380-380)
See ACTIVE WIRETAPPING and PASSIVE 2) WIRETAPPING.
work factor
1) An estimate of the effort or time needed to
overcome a protective measure by a potential penetrator with specified expertise and resources. (AR 380-380)
2) An estimate of the effort or time that can be expected to be expended to overcome a protective measure by a would-be penetrator with specified expertise and resources. (FIPS PUB 39)
3) An estimate of the effort or time needed by a potential penetrator with specified expertise and resources to overcome a protective measure. (NCSC-TG-004’88)
write
A fundamental operation that results only in the
flow of information from a subject to an object. (DOD 5200.28-STD)
write access
Permission to write an object. (DOD 5200.28-STD)
NOTE: There are no terms beginning with the letter "X".

The Glossary of Computer Security Terminology provides a summary of frequently encountered computer and communications security terms and various definitions used by federal agencies for those terms. This glossary does not provide a single definition per term; rather it reflects the variations in use of these terms among federal organizations.
